brief.topic: Open-source projects similar to the yc-software/qm multiplayer agent harness

criteria.question: Compared with qm's multiplayer agent harness for work, does the project expose people, teams, personal/shared scopes, isolated workspaces, Slack or web channels, group messages, projects, roles, and admin boundaries?

Compared with qm's ability to switch Pi, OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code behind one core, how does the project run agents, and how replaceable are models, harnesses, providers, sessions, and runtime adapters?

Compared with qm's Strict, Auto, and Dangerous security postures, per-scope durable sandbox, execute tool, credentials, approvals, and command policy, how does the project execute model-generated code or tools and enforce isolation?

Compared with qm's Postgres sessions, memory, queue, per-scope files and keychain view, how are conversations, files, memory, retrieval, artifacts, and durable state persisted and scoped, and what is the source of truth?

Compared with qm's channels, group messages, projects, crons, watches, inbound webhooks, and background work, what human-agent or agent-agent collaboration primitives exist for tasks, queues, delegation, workflows, messages, review, and scheduling?

Compared with qm's deployment directory and qm init flow for Fly or AWS in an operator-owned cloud account, what deployment and operations model does the project require for local or hosted runtime, databases, workers, schedulers, upgrades, and ownership?

Compared with qm's web apps, scope-owned skills, MCP or connector seams, plugins, HTTP API, Slack/web surfaces, and deployment layers, which plugins, tools, APIs, SDKs, UIs, provider seams, licenses, and package boundaries enable unit-capability composition?

Compared with qm's audit trail, security screening, live verification, CI, and operational checks, what audit, tracing, telemetry, evaluation, health, reliability, cost, or failure-recovery evidence can an operator use to know the system is healthy?

Compared with qm init's first-run deployment, Slack/web setup, scoped work, and live verification, what first-run experience, reference workflow, demo, or production deployment evidence shows the project can deliver useful work without adopting an entire platform?
